title: Treasury Prime Promotes Travis Champion to Chief Revenue Officer
summary: Treasury Prime is the operating platform for banks in the fintech era. A multi-bank network: 20+ banks, $1.1T in combined assets, 4 million active accounts.
body_markdown:
**SAN FRANCISCO, November 23, 2026** – Treasury Prime today announced the promotion of Travis Champion to Chief Revenue Officer. Champion was appointed Vice President of Revenue earlier this year to lead sales and marketing. As CRO, he now leads Bank and Fintech Sales, Marketing and Growth Marketing, Relationship Management and Client Services.


The expanded role puts the full partner relationship under one leader. Banks and fintechs will work with one team that is accountable from the first conversation through launch and long-term growth.


Under Champion, the revenue team has signed new fintech programs with several bank partners and expanded existing bank relationships with additional functionality. The team has also raised the quality of the fintech introductions it sends to banks. More later-stage fintechs are reaching more banks, and more of them are getting a response.


The promotion follows a year of momentum for Treasury Prime. In 2026, the company:


- Surpassed $170 billion in trailing annual payment volume, across more than 100 million transactions
- Launched Prime Cash, powered by Green Dot®, which lets fintech customers deposit cash at more than 90,000 retail locations nationwide
- Added Coastal and i3 Bank to a network of more than 20 banks with more than $1.1 trillion in combined assets
- Was listed by the Federal Reserve as a Fedwire Funds Service vendor, as both a service provider and a software provider
- Joined the Jack Henry Fintech Integration Network (FIN), Jack Henry's program for integrating with its core platforms and complementary solutions


Treasury Prime also brought its view to policymakers and regulators this fall. In November, CEO Chris Dean spoke on the embedded finance infrastructure panel at the American Fintech Council's 10th annual Policy Summit in Washington, D.C., where Champion also represented the company. The same month, Treasury Prime presented to regulators and technology leaders at the AIR / AFC Bridge Builders Conference at Kennesaw State University. The conference, hosted by the Alliance for Innovative Regulation and the American Fintech Council, focused on understanding the emerging technologies and risks of today and preparing for those of tomorrow.


“Travis has shown impressive leadership in bringing our sales and marketing teams together and giving the company one commercial plan,” said Chris Dean, CEO of Treasury Prime. “The next step is to put the whole partner relationship under his leadership. Our banks and fintechs should have one team accountable for their growth on Treasury Prime, from the day we meet them to the years after launch. Travis has earned that responsibility.”


As CRO, Champion will focus on growing the number of qualified banks and fintechs in the Treasury Prime network and on helping existing partners launch and expand programs. More than 3,600 fintechs are seeking a bank partner through the company's marketplace. He will also continue to build the AI-powered revenue engine he began as Vice President of Revenue.


“Signing a new bank or fintech is where the work starts,” said Travis Champion, Chief Revenue Officer at Treasury Prime. “Growth on this network comes from programs that launch, perform and expand. With sales, marketing, relationship management and client services working from one plan, we can stay with a partner at every stage. My focus is more qualified banks and fintechs in the network, and more value for each of them once they are here.”


Champion brings more than 25 years of experience leading sales and marketing organizations across fintech and financial services. Before Treasury Prime, he served as Head of GTM, Partnerships & Business Development at Minna Technologies. There he led the company's North America launch and grew its reach to more than 100 million U.S. cardholders, culminating in Minna's acquisition by Mastercard in 2024.


**About Treasury Prime**


Treasury Prime is an embedded banking platform that connects banks and fintechs. Banks use Treasury Prime to launch and oversee fintech programs through a bank-direct model. Fintechs use one integration to reach a network of more than 20 banks. The platform supports more than 4 million accounts and more than $170 billion in annual payment volume. Treasury Prime was founded in 2017 and is based in San Francisco. Learn more at[treasuryprime.com](https://www.treasuryprime.com/) .
